claims.claim: Exact stationary rarity. For 0<p<1, put α=1-p. If π is the stationary law, then the complete-state probability is Π_{n,p}:=π([n])=∏_{r=1}^n [rα^r/(n-(n-r)α^r)]. Equivalently, R_{n,p}:=Π_{n,p}^{-1}=∏_{r=1}^n [1+(n/r)(α^{-r}-1)].
claims.evidence: For 0<p<1 the finite chain is irreducible and its unique stationary law is permutation invariant. For a fixed r-set A, stationarity and the gain-then-loss update give M_r=α^r[(1-r/n)M_r+(r/n)M_{r-1}]: an outside draw requires A already present, while a draw i∈A requires A\{i} present, and all r members must survive. Solving and iterating from M_0=1 gives the first product and M_n=π([n]). Direct factor algebra gives its stated reciprocal. An independent exact stationary solve matched both products and every containment moment in all 852 rational test instances.
claims.search_method: Derived the stationary containment recursion directly from the source model, then independently constructed and solved the rational size-chain stationary system over n=1,...,12 and every reduced α with denominator at most 15.

claims.claim: Finite-n hitting-time sandwich. Let H_n=∑_{j=1}^n 1/j and A_{n,p}:=(R_{n,p}-1)/(1-α^n). Then for every n and 0<p<1, A_{n,p}≤E[T_{n,p}]≤H_n A_{n,p}.
claims.evidence: Writing h_k for the hitting mean from size k and e_k=h_k-h_{k+1}, upward skip-freeness identifies e_k with the k-to-(k+1) passage mean. A common-draw/common-survival coupling of nested sets preserves inclusion and a gap of at most one, proving e_k≤e_{k+1}. First-step analysis gives u_ke_k=1+Σ_{r<k}e_rF_k(r), u_k=(n-k)α^{k+1}/n. For coupled one-step sizes X≤Y≤X+1, a pointwise count proves Σ_{r=j}^{k-1}F_k(r)≥Σ_{r=j}^{k-2}F_{k-1}(r). Abel summation with the nonnegative increments of e_r therefore makes the recurrence numerator nondecreasing, so (n-k)e_k is nondecreasing and h_0≤H_ne_{n-1}. Kac's return identity gives R=1+Σ_{k<n}P_n(K_1=k)h_k; conditioning on K_1<n makes A a convex combination of h_0,...,h_{n-1}. Thus e_{n-1}≤A≤h_0≤H_ne_{n-1}≤H_nA. Exact direct hitting-time solves confirmed every identity and inequality in 852 rational instances, including n=1.
claims.search_method: Re-derived the passage recurrence, both coupling monotonicities, Abel comparison, and Kac decomposition; separately solved the transient rational linear systems and searched a broad finite grid for violations.

claims.claim: Asymptotic closure throughout the non-classical range. For every fixed η>0, uniformly over η(log n)/n²≤p_n<1, E[T_{n,p_n}]=(1+o(1))A_{n,p_n}=(1+o(1))(R_{n,p_n}-1)/(1-(1-p_n)^n).
claims.evidence: The passage recurrence yields e_k/e_{k-1}≥F_k(k-1)/u_k≥k(1-α^k)/[(n-k)α^{k+1}], using the event that a held coupon is drawn and at least one of the k held coupons is lost. With m=⌊n/2⌋ and β=m(1-α^m), the assumed lower bound on p gives β≥c_η log n uniformly: use 1-e^{-mp}≥mp/2 when mp≤1 and 1-e^{-mp}≥1-e^{-1} otherwise. For a_j=e_{n-j}/e_{n-1} and J=⌊β/2⌋, a_{j+1}≤(j/β)a_j for j<J, so Σ_{j=2}^J a_j=O(1/β) and a_J≤β^{-1}2^{-J+2}. Monotonicity of (n-k)e_k gives ja_j≤Ja_J for j≥J, whose harmonic tail is O(2^{-J}log n)=o_η(1). Hence h_0/e_{n-1}=1+o_η(1) uniformly. Since e_{n-1}≤A≤h_0 and E[T]=h_0, the claimed uniform equivalences follow. Exact checking confirmed all finite recurrence, ratio, and monotonicity premises on 852 rational instances.
claims.search_method: Proved the uniform passage-ratio tail estimate with explicit dependence on β and η, checked the full p-range including p approaching 1, and exact-tested all finite premises on a rational grid.

claims.claim: The resulting regimes differ from the product-of-marginals prediction. (i) If p=γ(log n)/n² with fixed γ>0, then E[T_{n,p}]∼n^{γ+1}/(γ log n). (ii) If (log n)/n²≪p≪1/n, then log E[T_{n,p}]∼n²p. (iii) If p=c/n with fixed c>0, then n^{-1}log E[T_{n,p}]→I(c):=∫_0^1 log(1+(e^{cx}-1)/x)dx>log(1+c). (iv) If np→∞, then log E[T_{n,p}]∼(n²/2)log(1/(1-p)).
claims.evidence: For p=o(1/n), uniform expansion of the product gives log R=n²p+O(n³p²). At p=γlog n/n² the error is o(1), so R∼n^γ and 1-α^n∼γlog n/n, proving (i). In (ii), n²p→∞, the relative product error is O(np)=o(1), and |log(np)|=o(n²p), so neither R-1 nor the denominator changes the logarithmic equivalent. For p=c/n, setting d_n=-nlog(1-c/n) gives d_n→c and the product sum is a Riemann sum for the stated continuous integrand; e^{cx}-1>cx for x>0 proves I(c)>log(1+c). Finally, with ℓ=-log α, exact factorization gives log R=n(n+1)ℓ/2+nlog n-log(n!)+Σ_r log(1-(1-r/n)e^{-rℓ}). The correction magnitude is at most Σ_{r≥1}-log(1-e^{-rℓ})=Σ_{q≥1}[q(e^{qℓ}-1)]^{-1}≤π²/(6ℓ). If np→∞, then nℓ→∞, so this correction and the O(n) factorial term are o(n²ℓ), proving (iv) after applying Claim 2. The checker independently verified the exact rational product factorization used here.
claims.search_method: Audited each asymptotic regime separately, retaining the R-1 and exit-probability corrections, proving the Riemann-sum limit and strict inequality, and deriving a uniform analytic bound for the large-loss correction.
